Whether you are a prospective parent/carer or pupil or existing member of our community, I hope that the information you find within the website will provide you with all the information you need and reflect what a committed, warm and happy community we are.
We value our pupils’ achievements in all areas of school life and all children are encouraged to strive, flourish and reach their full potential. However, our Christian values are at the heart of what we do and we pride ourselves on being an inclusive, happy and forward-looking school.

pageCache.pageTitle: All Saints' Church of England Primary School, Putney - Vision and Values
pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
Our school vision is built on strong foundations of faith, Christian values, and a long-standing tradition of care and excellence, uniting us around a shared purpose: to inspire, grow, and flourish as a school family for the future.
We have recently developed our school vision and added additional value and integrity by listening to the voices of children, staff, governors, and families. We wanted to ensure that we reflect on the past while embracing the present, ensuring our vision reflects the world our children live in today. We are rooted in faith and community, aiming to nurture confident and compassionate learners who are equipped to thrive in a changing and diverse society.

pageCache.pageTitle: All Saints' Church of England Primary School, Putney - British Values
pageCache.text:
British Values
Fundamental British Values Statement
The Department of Education requires schools ‘actively promote’ the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs.
At All Saints’ Church of England primary school these sit within the context of a church school where we are committed to promoting distinctively Christian values, which we strive to live out and teach day by day. Our Core Values of Kindness, Respect and Resilience are supplemented by many others including tolerance, courage, friendship.
We see British values as ‘values for living in Britain’ and shared human values, part of living well together harmoniously. We aim that the concepts and values of equality and justice, freedom and responsibility and love should support pupils to “develop wisdom, have hope, live well in community and demonstrate dignity”. (British Values in Church Schools, Pamela Draycott, 2016)
In this way, we believe we will prepare pupils for life in modern Britain and enable them to flourish as children of God.
“I have come that you might have life – life in all its fullness.” John 10:10
In this way, we will be contributing to the living out of The Church of England Vision for Education “Deeply Christian, Serving the Common Good”.
Promoting British Values - What does this look like in our school?
We provide opportunities for all pupils to explore and celebrate their own culture and that of others. We encourage all children to be tolerant and respectful to those of different faiths, or no faith, and their beliefs. This is done by providing the children with an understanding of main festivals and key dates of significant to British culture. e.g. Remembrance Day, the Queen’s Birthday and Jubilee celebrations and major political events such as elections.
How do we promote Democracy?
How do we promote the Rule of Law?
How do we promote Individual Liberty?
How do we promote Mutual Respect?
How do we promote Tolerance of those with different Faiths and Beliefs?
As well as promoting British Values, we will actively challenge pupils, staff, or parents expressing opinions contrary to fundamental British values including ‘extremist views’.
British Values

Our Faith Group plays an important role in strengthening the Christian life of All Saints’. Working with Mrs Ghosh, our Headteacher, and Rev Daniel Trott, pupils help to shape and lead Collective Worship, contribute to special church services and share their views on RE, faith and spirituality.

pageCache.pageTitle: All Saints' Church of England Primary School, Putney - All Saints' Church and Parish
pageCache.text:
All Saints' Church and Parish
All Saints’ CE Primary School is a Church of England Christian community in which we try to live out our faith in everything that we do and teach. We are fortunate to have very strong links with our church and our incumbent, enabling us to benefit from active and engaging Christian education and worship.
All Saints’ School seeks to follow a similar ethos to All Saints’ Church from which we take our name. Both church and school are inclusive Christian communities who seek to welcome and nurture everyone who wishes to be a part of the worshipping community. Together we try to support and nurture all children, staff and parents by providing equal respect and opportunity to everyone regardless of race, physical ability, gender, sexuality or creed.
The age old tradition of Anglican Church schools sees both school and church as a hub for the community whether children or adults, Christian or not. We seek to involve ourselves in community service as a part of our Christian witness. It is by working together with our community and worshipping together in school and church that we are disciples of Jesus.
Worship plays a huge part in the life of All Saints’ School. The Vicar, the Reverend Daniel Trott leads Collective Worship in the school on a regular, half-termly basis. We also meet in church for major festivals and monthly for the School Eucharist, to which parents and other members of the school community are warmly invited. The Vicar of All Saints’ is a familiar face around the school and is a school governor. He also meets regularly with the Headteacher and the Faith Group within the school. Our main concern is to teach Christianity in a way that is clear and relevant to today’s world and to encourage children and adults alike, to use the great Christian stories and the great themes of the Christian year to interpret their own lives and their own experiences.
Our mission is not so much to teach children about the Christian faith but to teach them to use their Christian faith in every aspect of their lives as they grow and develop. Hopefully, we do this by example and encouragement. Our aim is that All Saints’ School lives out its Christianity in the classroom and the playground, in school and in church, week by week and year by year, providing a firm foundation for happy, healthy and creative learning and development for every child in the school.

pageCache.pageTitle: All Saints' Church of England Primary School, Putney - Welcome
pageCache.text:
Welcome
Welcome to All Saints' CE Primary School.
On behalf of the members of All Saints' CE Primary School, I warmly welcome you to our website. Whether you are a prospective parent/carer or pupil or existing member of our community, I hope that the information you find within the website will provide you with all the information you need and reflect what a committed, warm and happy community we are.
We value our pupils’ achievements in all areas of school life and all children are encouraged to strive, flourish and reach their full potential. However, our Christian values are at the heart of what we do and we pride ourselves on being an inclusive, happy and forward-looking school.
As you will see, community and relationships are integral to the life and success of All Saints’ and our enthusiastic and hard-working pupils, staff, governors and parents work together to provide a broad range of rich opportunities to broaden, extend and deepen the children’s learning.
In partnership with parents and children, we promote personal development, positive attitudes towards all aspects of school life and others and a respect for the richness of all cultures. Children leave All Saints’ as interesting, knowledgeable, curious and kind young people, ready for their next steps in learning.
We are continually reflecting, striving forward in the pursuit of excellence, and I am proud and privileged to lead our wonderful school.
For all prospective parents, you are warmly invited to contact the school office to arrange and visit where you will receive a very warm welcome, feel the caring ethos which is so important to us, and see for yourself that All Saints’ is the place for your child.

pageCache.pageTitle: All Saints' Church of England Primary School, Putney - Reception Maths Workshop
pageCache.text:
Reception Maths Workshop
This morning, Reception parents joined Mrs Grantcharova for an informative and interactive Maths Workshop exploring how mathematics is taught at All Saints’.
Mrs Grantcharova explained what maths learning looks like for Reception-aged children and how we develop strong mathematical foundations through practical experiences, exploration, mathematical talk and carefully structured activities. Parents also had the opportunity to get hands-on with a maths task themselves, experiencing the types of activities our children encounter in the classroom!
The session provided lots of practical ideas for supporting mathematical development at home, as well as an opportunity for parents to ask questions and learn more about our approach.
Thank you to everyone who joined us and to Mrs Grantcharova for leading such a valuable session. Working together helps us give our youngest mathematicians the confidence, curiosity and strong foundations they need to flourish.

Early Years, KS1 and KS2 Results
All Saints' School Performance Tables Page
School and College Performance Tables Service
All Saints’ CE Primary School Results
At All Saints’ we are extremely proud of our school's high academic achievements, which ensure that our pupils move onto the next stage of their education very well prepared. Please do look at the list of Leavers’ Destinations of our Year 6 pupils in the Information section of the website, to see details of all the schools at which our children get places.
KS2 RESULTS 2025
Pupils in Year 6 take SATS tests. These tests are used to ascertain whether children are working at the ‘Expected Standard’ or are working above this, at ‘Greater Depth’. They also give an average score, comparing the results to national averages, with 100 being the threshold for the ‘Expected Standard’.
FOUNDATION STAGE PROFILE
Attainment is shown in two ways: Good Level of Development (GLD) and an Average Score. As you can see, children commencing their statutory education at All Saints’, get off to the best possible start, achieving higher than children both in the Local Authority and nationally. The Foundation Stage data is the culmination of continuous assessment throughout the year.

Wraparound Care
All Saints’ is partnered with 'The Play Professionals' to provide on-site comprehensive wraparound childcare services for our school community. We will be offering the following services:
Breakfast Club – 7.30am – 8.45am / £5.50 per session (ad-hoc booking £8.00*)
After School Club – 3.15pm – 6pm / £15.50 per session (ad-hoc booking £20.00*)
*Flexible, last-minute bookings are perfect for unexpected work commitments or family needs. After-school club can be booked up to 3pm on the day, and Breakfast Club up to 7:15am on the day.
For more information about accessing these services and to register online, please visit https://playp.org.uk/
